summary: Reading Room specimen: one self-contained HTML file staging the essay-and-margin thesis — editorial column with numerals 1-4, ruled gutter notes with in-place expansion, summoned Files sheet citing Notes 2-3, quiet in-place failure with retry, empty-session colophon, streaming caret, and full-bleed sheet behavior at 375px.

claims.claim: First view resolves the hierarchy: measure-constrained editorial article column with marginal evidence numerals in the gutter, slim withdrawn session rail (left) and evidence rail (right), and a calm composer with ordered follow-ups.

Marginal-numeral signature is in place and in use: superscript numerals 1-4 inside assistant prose match ruled gutter notes 1-4, and the summoned verification sheet header cites the same range (Notes 2-3, Files view).
Central component works: marginal note 2 expands in place from summary to evidence detail (paths, command, duration, status label) without cards or navigation.
Non-happy states render at full calm in place: tool failure row with persistent label plus retry (never a toast), an empty-session colophon with one next action, and a streaming caret line.

Editorial typography and warm-paper-plus-glass surfaces hold at reading density: serif essay at true text size, small sans chrome, mono quarantined to code and evidence, hairline rules, dark code wells, one sheet level above the page.

Responsive behavior is specified in a working media query: gutters collapse to footnote rows, rails become drawers, and summoned sheets go full-bleed at 375px with no horizontal scroll and a persistently reachable composer.

Eligibility: specimen is reference-only (required comment is the first bytes), fully self-contained (inline CSS only, zero external assets, tiny disclosure script that works from file://), and covers all six required elements (a)-(f) with stubbed sessions, tool trace, both rails, and the non-happy state present.

decisions.choice: Render one combined self-contained specimen file that stages all six evidence-plan beats in reading order: first view, signature with summoned sheet, expanded marginal note, in-place failure plus empty plus streaming states, density passage, and responsive rules.
rationale: One file keeps the citation thread (numerals 1-4 across prose, margin, and sheet header) judgeable in a single viewport.
The assignment requires ONE self-contained HTML specimen covering (a)-(f).
alternatives: Six separate files, one per evidence-plan beat
risks: A single long file can read as a page rather than a system; rails, sheet, and footnote collapse carry the system reading.
revisitWhen: The coordinator splits specimens per evidence-plan beat

risks: Static stub limitation: the summoned sheet is staged open for judgment; in the product it appears only when called from a numeral and dismisses back to the unbroken page.
Static stub limitation: retry, streaming caret, and drawer toggles are illustrative client-only stubs with synthetic data; no real latency, tool execution, or session switching occurs.
Footnote rows duplicate gutter-note content so narrow-viewport behavior is judgeable without resizing; a build would render one source through two presentations, not two copies.

Numeral fatigue ceiling: turns with many consequential calls must cap inline numerals and collapse to a labeled range (e.g. notes 3-7); this specimen shows four notes and does not prove the collapsed-range presentation.
Quiet-failure risk: breath motion and warm grounds can soften urgency; the persistent label-plus-retry row must carry the weight that pulse and toast normally carry.
